Personality: Pryndor is a classic Battanian hardman whose character brims with the wildness and ruthlessness of the hill folk. As the leader of Clan fen Morcar, he believes in the supremacy of strength, leading from the front on the battlefield and winning renown as a warrior through extraordinary grit and accomplished archery. Yet his nature is devoid of mercy; he treats captives and defiers with extreme cruelty, earning a reputation for brutality known throughout the kingdom. Uninterested in intricate political calculation or generous charity, he prefers to settle problems directly by force of arms. In his view, Battania's survival requires not weak-kneed sympathy, but unyielding will and lethal strikes. Guarding his authority as chieftain with near-obsessive vigilance, he crushes any challenge to his standing without pity as a dreaded, iron-fisted lord.
Background: Pryndor hails from the prominent Battanian house of fen Morcar, serving as its current clan leader from the family seat of Llanoc Hen Castle. Under the rule of High King Caladog, though he has sworn fealty, in his bones he retains the fiercely independent spirit of a traditional Battanian chieftain who believes that his lands and people belong to him alone. Having spent his entire life campaigning through deep mountains and dense forests, he is a master of the longbow and close-combat weapons alike, ranking among the kingdom's finest woodland hunters and tacticians. Father to four children—Floraidh, Beitrin, Diabhain, and Branoc—he raises them with a harsh hand in an effort to pass down the clan's power. Whatever criticisms his brutal conduct draws abroad, he has successfully defended his family's fiefs amid turbulent times and continues to hold a firm place in Battania's power structure through sheer toughness.
